header.eyebrow: Finance Technology · State as of 2023, not current · Oracle Fusion Cloud
header.title: Insurance Estate Map
header.lede: Policy administration, payroll, procurement and banking feed one Oracle ledger per entity; a finance data warehouse on ADW and Enterprise EPM sit around it for reporting, planning and close. Select any system to see what it does, how it connects and where to read more.

footer: Source: finance-technology notebook 2020–2023 (anonymised). Shows the state as of 2023, not the current state.

legend.label: Data Integration / Data Management / file load

nodes.title: Policy administration
nodes.subtitle: Exceed · premium & claims
nodes.description: The insurance system of record for policies, premium, commission, claims and case reserves.
functions: Issues, renews and cancels policies; bills premium and pays commission
Records claims, losses and case reserves
Reporting data lands in the on-premise warehouse, then reaches the ADW insurance data mart through OCI Data Integration
Its activity reaches the ledger as daily Premium, Loss and Claims journals

nodes.title: Payroll
nodes.subtitle: ADP
nodes.description: Payroll processing; produces the payroll journal file for the ledger.
functions: Runs payroll per pay period
Produces a GL file with pay codes mapped to Oracle accounts
Target path: SFTP → OIC → GL (legacy: manual upload)

nodes.title: Corporate card
nodes.subtitle: Visa
nodes.description: Corporate card programme feeding employee expenses.
functions: Daily card transaction file
Loaded directly into Oracle Expenses without a decryption server
Card transactions become expense report lines

nodes.title: Investments
nodes.subtitle: Clearwater · planned
nodes.description: Investment accounting for the bond and equity portfolio; journal interface planned at go-live.
functions: Investment accounting and portfolio reporting
Journals to GL planned through OIC
Investment P&L reported separately in Financial Reporting

nodes.title: Oracle HCM
nodes.subtitle: workers · directory
nodes.description: Oracle HCM Cloud: the worker record used by Expenses, approvals and single sign-on.
functions: Holds workers, managers and departments used by approval hierarchies
Integrates with Expenses for employee data
Sends daily change and weekly full worker extracts for directory accounts and single sign-on

nodes.title: On-premise data warehouse
nodes.subtitle: EDW · BIM · HDS · DWM (SQL Server)
nodes.description: On-premise SQL Server data stores: the enterprise data warehouse (EDW), the BIM reporting database with Exceed policy data, and HDS. None of them is Essbase.
functions: EDW: enterprise data warehouse; the Finance workgroup database feeds Tableau reports and receives the budget
BIM / DWM: policy, premium (GWP, EP, UEP), claims and losses, loss reserves, subrogation and salvage
HDS: data store; some reports sourced from Db2 through it
Feeds ADW through OCI Data Integration (previously DataSync)

nodes.title: DocuSign
nodes.subtitle: eSignature
nodes.description: DocuSign eSignature for internal agreements across departments (not Claims); not part of the dashboard flow.
functions: Organisation → account → group structure with three sub-accounts (one for the Agency)
Single sign-on through Azure AD; about 70 active users; external accounts cleaned up
Offboarding checklist covers DocuSign documents and contract ownership

nodes.title: Oracle Integration Cloud
nodes.subtitle: orchestrations · REST · SOAP
nodes.description: The integration platform for scheduled and event-driven flows into and out of Fusion.
functions: Invokes BI Publisher reports and loads the output into ADW tables
Runs the ERP bulk-extract pattern (ESS job, business event, download)
Updates suppliers through REST (business classifications)
Carries payroll and planned investment journals into GL

nodes.title: Workiva (OneCloud)
nodes.subtitle: ETL · scheduler (non-Oracle)
nodes.description: Workiva (OneCloud): the third-party integration studio and data-prep tool used for ETL between the finance Oracle cloud systems.
functions: Moves GL trial balances and actuals/budget into Planning, and Planning into the OAC Essbase cubes
Sends allocations and statistical allocation rates back to GL; loads the budget to the on-premise EDW
Publishes report outputs to the Financials Doc Cloud; runs the EPM backups
Connectors for OTBI, ADW, Financials Cloud, ARCS, OAC, Planning, SQL Server, Db2, SFTP; review planned to replace them with Data Integration and OIC

nodes.title: EPM Data Management
nodes.subtitle: GL ↔ EPM
nodes.description: EPM's integration layer between the Fusion ledger and the EPM applications.
functions: Loads GL actuals into Planning (and the close application)
Exports budget and statistical journals back to GL budget balances
Maps Fusion COA members to EPM dimensions

nodes.title: File loaders
nodes.subtitle: FBDI · spreadsheets · REST
nodes.description: Standard Oracle bulk loaders used for journals, conversions and master data.
functions: Journal import for the daily policy journals after Financial Integrator mapping
Spreadsheet loaders for journals, budgets and segment values / hierarchies
Go-live conversions: 5 years of GL balances, suppliers, assets, open POs, contracts

nodes.title: OCI Data Integration
nodes.subtitle: Fast Connect
nodes.description: OCI Data Integration ("Fast Connect"): the connection from on-premise Exceed data to ADW for FP&A, replacing DataSync.
functions: Loads Exceed policy data from the on-premise warehouse into the ADW insurance data mart
Converted the BIM reports, including six-month auto policy reporting, and allowed BIM to retire
Treated as implemented (successor to the DataSync VM)

nodes.title: Integration VM
nodes.subtitle: DataSync · Data Gateway · GroundRunner
nodes.description: On-premise Windows VM that hosted the legacy connectors between on-premise data and Oracle Cloud.
functions: DataSync: BIM to the ADW insurance data mart (legacy)
Oracle Data Gateway: on-premise data to OAC
GroundRunner: Workiva (OneCloud) agent and EPM automation; services needed a check after monthly patching

nodes.title: Suppliers
nodes.subtitle: registration · qualification
nodes.description: The supplier master with registration, qualification and enrichment.
functions: Supplier registration with approval for prospective and internal suppliers
Qualification questionnaires score business classifications (diversity)
DataFox enriches supplier firmographics
An OIC interface updates business classifications through REST
An APEX app maintains qualification questions through REST

nodes.title: Procurement & contracts
nodes.subtitle: requisitions · agreements
nodes.description: Self-Service Procurement, purchasing agreements and supplier contracts.
functions: Requisitions approved by amount tier (to 5K, 50K, 100K, 250K, over 250K)
Blanket and contract purchase agreements; agreement change orders can auto-approve
Supplier contracts (MSA, CSA, SOW, NDA) with signed PDFs in Enterprise Contracts
Home-page tile for contracts expiring this week

nodes.title: Purchasing & receipts
nodes.subtitle: POs · accruals
nodes.description: Purchase orders and receipts; uninvoiced receipts accrue at period end.
functions: Purchase orders from requisitions and agreements
Receipts against POs (three-way match)
Period-end chain: transfer to costing, then Create Uninvoiced Receipt Accruals
Only received-over-invoiced amounts accrue; finally closed POs drop off the accrual report

nodes.title: Payables & imaging
nodes.subtitle: invoices · approvals
nodes.description: Supplier invoices captured by email and OCR, matched, and approved by amount tier.
functions: Integrated Invoice Imaging (OCR): invoices by email, imported hourly to Payables
OCR accuracy was weak: automatic validation was held for the Mutual and the Agency and AP validated manually
Planned move to Oracle Intelligent Document Recognition (IDR), the AI-based engine for images and email
Approval by amount tier; over 250K to an approval group; PO-matched and recurring invoices auto-approve

nodes.title: Payments & cash
nodes.subtitle: Bank A · BAI2
nodes.description: Payment runs, bank files and bank statement reconciliation.
functions: Payment process requests with payment approval by approval group
ACH and control-totals file, and Positive Pay for printed checks, to Bank A over SFTP
BAI2 bank statements reconciled in Cash Management (new with Fusion)

nodes.title: Expenses
nodes.subtitle: card · out of pocket
nodes.description: Employee expense reports, fed by the corporate card and HCM.
functions: Corporate card transactions loaded daily
Expense approval with an override-approver privilege
Approved reports become Payables invoices

nodes.title: Fixed Assets
nodes.subtitle: assets
nodes.description: Asset subledger fed from Payables.
functions: Additions from Payables
Depreciation by book
Closed on business day 3–4

nodes.title: Intercompany & allocations
nodes.subtitle: Mutual ↔ Agency
nodes.description: Intercompany billing between the Mutual and the Agency, and allocation rules.
functions: Monthly shared-services billing from the Mutual to the Agency through Oracle Intercompany
Receiving organisation approves; batches transfer to GL; settlement clears receivable and payable
Allocation rule sets (source, target, range, basis, offset) post to allocation companies 81–89

nodes.title: Subledger Accounting
nodes.subtitle: rules engine
nodes.description: One accounting engine for Payables, Purchasing receipts, Payments and Assets.
functions: Journal entry rule sets, account rules and mapping sets per subledger
Creates accounting for accruals, invoices, payments and assets
Transfers to GL by category

nodes.title: General Ledger
nodes.subtitle: Mutual · Agency · 8-segment COA
nodes.description: The ledgers for the Mutual and the Agency, on one 8-segment chart of accounts.
functions: Company, Department, Account, Product, State, Class, Project, Intercompany
Hierarchies published to the GL balances cube for FRS, Smart View and OTBI
About six allocation rules a month in Calculation Manager; payroll allocations post by state
Closed on business day 6; statutory balance sheet shows surplus
Segment value security and cross-validation rules

nodes.title: Enterprise EPM
nodes.subtitle: close · planning · reconciliation
nodes.description: Oracle Enterprise EPM: close task manager, planning, narrative reporting, reconciliation, tax reporting.
functions: Planning: Financials, Workforce and Reporting Essbase cubes (plus Capital and Strategic Planning cubes)
Financial Consolidation and Close used as the month-end close checklist (consolidation planned)
Account Reconciliation (2021/22) and Narrative Reporting packages (about 200 reports)
Enterprise Data Management (future); Financial Reporting & Compliance for model-audit-rule and internal-audit controls
Migrated to the Enterprise EPM bundle in 2022

nodes.title: Autonomous Data Warehouse
nodes.subtitle: Oracle Autonomous Database
nodes.description: Oracle Autonomous Database (Data Warehouse workload): the Finance Transaction Data Warehouse, holding transaction-level data from Fusion, PeopleSoft history and policy data. Not Essbase.
functions: Financial report mart of all Fusion transactional modules (live February 2021)
PeopleSoft Financials history
Insurance data mart (daily, monthly and stage schemas) fed from the on-premise warehouse through OCI Data Integration
Loaded from Fusion through OIC (BI Publisher reports, bulk extracts) and Workiva (OneCloud)
SQL checks reconcile daily policy journals and extracts to source; source for OAC dashboards and BI Publisher

nodes.title: Oracle Analytics Cloud
nodes.subtitle: BI · DV · Essbase · BI Publisher
nodes.description: Oracle Analytics Cloud: dashboards, the Essbase financials cube and data visualisation.
functions: Dynamic reporting: BI dashboards, Data Visualization and Smart View analytics
OAC Essbase cubes: Financials, Revenue Planning, Analytics, Foundation
Transactional dashboards from OTBI datasets and ADW through DV data flows
Static reporting for non-Essbase data with BI Publisher, against ADW and the on-premise warehouse

nodes.title: Fusion reporting
nodes.subtitle: OTBI · BIP · FRS · Smart View
nodes.description: Reporting inside Fusion: real-time analyses, pixel-perfect reports, financial statements and Excel analysis.
functions: OTBI: real-time subject areas for GL balances and journals, P2P, and subledger-to-ledger reconciliation
BI Publisher: custom reports and data models; replaced about 130 legacy reports with about 50
Financial Reporting Studio: about 20 statements, including statutory balance sheet, statement of surplus, P&L by product
Smart View: ad hoc analysis on the GL balances cube
Transactional KPIs: invoices processed and paid on time, PO-backed %, payment method mix

nodes.title: Bank A
nodes.subtitle: ACH · Positive Pay · BAI2
nodes.description: The operating bank: receives payment files, returns statements.
functions: Receives ACH and control-totals files over SFTP
Receives Positive Pay files for printed checks
Returns BAI2 statements daily
Validates test files in 48–72 hours; about 5 days to move a format to production

nodes.title: OCI tenancy
nodes.subtitle: usage & cost
nodes.description: The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure tenancy hosting ADW, OIC, OAC, Essbase, Data Integration and EPM.
functions: Usage and cost dashboard by service, maintained monthly
Stakeholders consulted to estimate future usage from their planned projects
Later replaced by Oracle's live OCI usage application; user and role provisioning through OCI IAM

p2p.title: Procure to Pay: eight stages
p2p.lede: Suppliers are registered and qualified, requisitions and invoices are approved by amount tier, and payments leave as bank files. Accounting starts with the period-end accrual; invoice and payment follow through Subledger Accounting.

stages.title: Supplier onboarding
points: Supplier registration with approval for prospective and internal suppliers
Qualification questionnaires score business classifications (diversity)
DataFox enriches supplier records; an OIC interface updates classifications through REST
Go-live converted all suppliers with 18 months of AP history and 1099 flags

stages.title: Requisition
points: Approval by amount tier: to 5K, 50K, 100K, 250K, and over 250K
Supervisory hierarchy with named exceptions
P-card on requisitions is limited: the PO is created closed for receiving and card details don't reach AP

stages.title: Purchase order & contracts
points: Purchase orders, blanket and contract purchase agreements
Agreement change orders can auto-approve
Supplier contracts (MSA, CSA, SOW, NDA) stored with signed PDFs
Home-page tile shows contracts expiring this week

stages.title: Receipt
points: Receipts against POs complete the three-way match
No accounting at receipt: uninvoiced receipts accrue at period end
Only received-over-invoiced amounts accrue
POs leave the accrual report only when finally closed

entries.event: Period end: receipts not yet invoiced

stages.title: Invoice
points: Invoices arrive by email, are read by OCR and imported to Payables
Approval by amount tier; over 250K to an approval group
PO-matched and recurring invoices auto-approve
Imaging audit (imported not validated, deleted, not imported) tracked in ADW and OAC

stages.title: Payment
points: Payment process requests with approval by approval group
ACH file built in Oracle and sent straight to the bank's SFTP
Printed checks with a Positive Pay file
Corporate card spend reaches Payables through Expenses

cr: Cash, or Cash clearing (option not documented)

stages.title: Settlement
points: Bank A receives ACH, control-totals and Positive Pay files
BAI2 statements return daily and are reconciled in Cash Management
New file formats: transmission test, content validation in 48–72 hours, about 5 days to production

stages.title: Monitoring
points: Invoices processed and paid on time; % of invoices with a PO
Payment method mix: check, ACH, manual
Requisitions and POs by source (requisition, agreement, contract); new contracts and suppliers
Payables-to-ledger reconciliation in OTBI

p2p.accounting_note: Account types follow the Oracle Payables 26C defaults. Expense items accrue at period end and reverse when the next period opens. Whether payments are accounted at clearing (cash clearing) is not documented.

notes.title: Approvals are amount tiers.
notes.text: Requisitions and invoices share the same tiers (5K, 50K, 100K, 250K); the top tier goes to an approval group.

r2r.title: Record to Report: eight stages
r2r.lede: Daily policy journals, payroll and subledger accounting land in the ledgers of the Mutual and the Agency; intercompany and allocations run monthly; the close is driven from the EPM close task manager and ends on business day 6.

stages.title: Journals in
points: Daily policy journals (Premium, Loss, Claims) from the insurance data mart via a Financial Integrator
Premium and commission one day in arrears; case reserves two days
Payroll journal from ADP, mapped to Oracle accounts
A back-load chain reruns a missed load date

stages.title: Intercompany
points: Monthly shared-services billing from the Mutual to the Agency
The receiving organisation approves; batches transfer to GL
Settlement clears the receivable and payable against cash

stages.title: Allocations
points: Rule sets define source, target, range, basis and offset
A fixed point of view holds the segments that don't move
Results post to the allocation companies 81–89

stages.title: Fixed assets
points: Additions from Payables
Depreciation by book
Closed on business day 3–4

stages.title: Period-end adjustments
points: Uninvoiced receipts accrued at period end
Journals in accrual and adjustment categories auto-reverse on the first day of the next period
Journal approval by approval group

stages.title: Ledger close
points: Business day 6; may reopen for late statutory entries
Statutory balance sheet shows surplus, not retained earnings; Mutual and Agency differ
Year end: opening the new year rolls revenue and expense into retained earnings per balancing segment, without a journal
New segment values and hierarchies are published to the GL balances cube

stages.title: Close management & reconciliation
points: Close task manager holds the calendar, owners and sign-off
Account Reconciliation for balance sheet accounts (since September 2021)
Payables and Receivables to Ledger reconciliation in OTBI

stages.title: Reporting & planning
points: About 20 FRS statements: statutory balance sheet, statement of surplus, P&L by product and state, cash flow
Foundation not-for-profit statements and Agency statements
Narrative Reporting packages with review and sign-off
Planning budgets and statistical journals return to GL budget balances

r2r.accounting_note: Intercompany entries come from the source notebook. Allocation, revaluation-free accrual and fixed-asset types follow the Oracle 26C guides and Oracle standard. Premium and loss entries are typical insurance accounting shown for illustration; the source does not document them.

notes.title: Statutory view.
notes.text: Statutory statements show surplus rather than retained earnings; the Statement of Surplus is an FRS report.

fnd.title: Foundation & controls
fnd.lede: The structures and rules every transaction passes through: the chart of accounts, hierarchies, security, accounting rules and approval workflows.

stages.title: Enterprise structure
points: Mutual (company 10) and Agency (company 20) ledgers in one data set
Foundation (company 90) reports as a not-for-profit
Statutory company 80 and allocation companies 81–89
New subsidiary: company value, hierarchy, legal entity, balancing segment, ledger and BU assignments

stages.title: Chart of accounts
points: Company, Department, Account, Product, State, Class, Project, Intercompany
Product (line of business) and State support statutory reporting
Accounting Scenario values hold actual and budget versions

stages.title: Hierarchies & cube
points: Account and segment trees audited, flattened and published to the balances cube
New values reach the cube through the cube-update process
Bulk changes through the segment values and hierarchies import
Alternate hierarchies for sales channel and statistical accounts

stages.title: Security & validation
points: Segment value security on cost center and account
Data access sets per ledger and business-unit access for subledgers
Cross-validation rules and combination sets
Custom roles trimmed from seeded job roles

stages.title: Accounting rules & mappings
points: Subledger Accounting rule sets, account rules and mapping sets
Financial Integrator maps policy activity to GL accounts
ADP pay codes map to GL accounts
EPM Data Management maps GL to Planning and close

stages.title: Approval workflows
points: Requisitions and invoices by amount tier (5K, 50K, 100K, 250K, over 250K)
Payments, journals and invoices over 250K by approval group
Supplier registration and spend-authorisation approvals
Workflow Rules Report documents the configured rules

stages.title: Journal controls
points: Auto-reverse by category to the first day of the next period
Journal approval by approval group
Close by module from business day 1 to 6

stages.title: Change & release
points: Oracle updates each quarter (March, June, September, December)
Regression list: integrations, OTBI subject areas, Essbase, Workiva (OneCloud) chains
Post-refresh steps after copying production to test

notes.title: Why this matters.
notes.text: Most reporting and integration issues trace back to a mapping, a hierarchy not yet published to the cube, or a validation rule.

onboarding.title: Data & reporting
onboarding.lede: ADW is the finance data warehouse; Enterprise EPM handles planning and close; OAC and the Fusion reporting tools serve users. Each lane is a path data takes from Oracle to a report.

steps.label: BI Publisher report
steps.text: Data model and report in Fusion define the extract

steps.label: OIC scheduled orchestration
steps.text: Invokes the report web service, stages the file, inserts rows into an ADW table

steps.label: Bulk extract
steps.text: ESS extract job → business event → download to object storage or FTP

steps.label: ADW
steps.text: Finance report mart; spot checks compare report output with the table

lanes.title: Policy data to the ledger
lanes.route: Exceed → BIM (SQL Server) → ADW insurance data mart → Financial Integrator → GL

steps.label: Exceed
steps.text: Premium, commission, claims and case reserves

steps.label: BIM (SQL Server, on-premise)
steps.text: Policy, premium and claims reporting data; a load server copies it to ADW

steps.label: Insurance data mart (ADW)
steps.text: Stage and temp tables by load date

steps.label: Financial Integrator
steps.text: Maps activity to GL accounts; journal categories Premium, Loss, Claims

steps.label: General Ledger
steps.text: Daily journals; SQL checks tie back to source

lanes.title: EPM and cubes
lanes.route: GL → Data Management → Planning → Workiva (OneCloud) → OAC Essbase

steps.label: Data Management
steps.text: GL actuals to Planning; budgets back to GL

steps.label: Workiva (OneCloud)
steps.text: Loads Planning financials and ADW metrics into the OAC Essbase cube; backups

steps.label: OAC
steps.text: Dashboards and Smart View on the Essbase cube

lanes.title: Reporting layer
lanes.route: OTBI · BI Publisher · FRS · Smart View · OAC

steps.label: OTBI
steps.text: Real-time subject areas; reconciliation subject areas

steps.label: BI Publisher
steps.text: Custom reports to a content-cloud folder for Accounting

steps.label: FRS & Smart View
steps.text: Financial statements and ad hoc analysis on the GL balances cube

notes.title: Four types of finance reporting.
notes.text: Operational (OTBI, BIP), management (EPM, Essbase), enterprise analytics (OAC on ADW), regulatory (statutory statements).

notes.title: Reconciliation points.
notes.text: Account Reconciliation; Payables/Receivables to Ledger in OTBI; policy-feed SQL checks by load date; before/after extract checks.

notes.title: ADW as the warehouse.
notes.text: ADW is an Oracle Autonomous Database (Data Warehouse workload) holding transaction-level finance data. Fusion data reaches it through OIC and Workiva (OneCloud), policy data through BIM; Data Sync was replaced by ODI / OCI Data Integration.

notes.title: Where Essbase sits.
notes.text: Two Essbase cubes: the OAC financials cube (from Planning via Workiva (OneCloud)) and the Fusion GL balances cube (FRS, Smart View, OTBI). EDW, BIM and HDS are SQL Server databases, and ADW is an Oracle Autonomous Database.

close.title: Close process
close.lede: Scheduled processes run the daily rhythm; at month end the subledgers close from business day 1 to 4, allocations and intercompany run, the GL closes on day 6, and FP&A publishes the dashboards. Select any step for details; the calendar follows below.

timeline.what: Create Accounting every 4 hours (subledgers 15 minutes apart); AutoPost every 8 hours
Import imaged invoices hourly; validate every 15 minutes (held for Mutual and Agency while OCR accuracy improved)
Initiate invoice approval workflow, per business unit
Create mass additions (Payables to Assets)
Refresh the GL balances cubes (Smart View, FRS, Planning loads)
BAI2 bank statements processed; autoreconcile at 10:00
Corporate card file uploaded; expense reimbursements every 12 hours
Policy journals: premium and commissions, claims, change in case reserves (OIC from ADW)
Payroll journal from ADP
Policy journals: policy count and average written, advanced premiums, written vs prior written
Receiving to costing → uninvoiced receipt accruals → report → Create Accounting (final); reverses next period
Payables and expense reports close
Cash Management close
Procurement and Payables close
Fixed Assets close
About six allocation rules (payroll by state); shared-services intercompany billing
General Ledger close; may reopen for late statutory entries
FP&A loads actuals into Planning once or twice a day until the P&Ls tie; account reconciliations
Dashboards and financial reports published; month announced closed
Oracle update: patch DEV, TEST covers production, then TEST and PROD; regression of integrations, OTBI reports and trial balance
Open the first period of the new year: revenue and expense roll to retained earnings

nodes.title: Invoice import & validation
nodes.subtitle: Payables · imaging
nodes.description: Imaged invoices enter Payables and are validated.
functions: Import Payables Invoices hourly from 01:00 per business unit (source: Invoice Image)
Validation every 15 minutes; held for the Mutual and the Agency while OCR accuracy was improved
Planned move from OCR to Intelligent Document Recognition (IDR)

nodes.title: Invoice approval
nodes.subtitle: workflow
nodes.description: Routes invoices to approvers by amount tier.
functions: Initiate Invoice Approval Workflow daily per business unit (04:25 / 04:30)
Tiers to 5K, 50K, 100K, 250K; over 250K to an approval group
PO-matched and recurring invoices auto-approve

nodes.title: Corporate card & expenses
nodes.subtitle: Expenses
nodes.description: Card transactions and expense reports become payables.
functions: Corporate card file uploaded and validated by OIC (08:00)
Process Expense Reimbursements and Cash Advances every 12 hours
Workers synced weekly with the card issuer
integrations: Upload and validate corporate card file

nodes.title: Bank statements
nodes.subtitle: Cash Management
nodes.description: Daily bank data and reconciliation.
functions: BAI2 statements from Bank A processed at 07:00
Autoreconcile Bank Statements at 10:00 per bank account
ACH and Positive Pay transmit automatically with payment runs

nodes.title: Policy journals
nodes.subtitle: OIC
nodes.description: Insurance operations activity booked to GL from ADW.
functions: Daily premium and commissions, claims, change in case reserves at 10:00
Monthly policy count, advanced premiums, written vs prior written in the first 5 days
Creates unposted batches; daily load status shown on a dashboard

nodes.title: Payroll journal
nodes.subtitle: ADP → GL
nodes.description: Bi-weekly payroll journal from ADP.
functions: ADP file loaded by OIC on Wednesdays, bi-weekly
Accounts mapped from ADP pay codes
State captured for payroll allocations

nodes.title: Create Accounting
nodes.subtitle: all subledgers
nodes.description: Subledger Accounting creates journal entries for every subledger.
functions: Every 4 hours from 02:00; per-subledger runs 15 minutes apart (rescheduled January 2022)
Multiperiod accounting hourly afterwards
Month end: final run for receipt accounting, transfer and post

nodes.title: AutoPost
nodes.subtitle: General Ledger
nodes.description: Posts journal batches periodically.
functions: AutoPost Journals every 8 hours from 02:00
Picks up subledger, policy and payroll batches
Journal approval by approval group for manual journals

nodes.title: Balances cube refresh
nodes.subtitle: GL → Essbase
nodes.description: Refreshes the GL balances cubes.
functions: Transfer General Ledger Balances to Balances Cube daily at 05:45
Feeds Smart View, Financial Reporting and the Planning loads
New segment values reach the cube through the cube-update process
integrations: Transfer GL Balances to Balances Cube

nodes.title: Mass additions
nodes.subtitle: Payables → Assets
nodes.description: Capital invoice lines become asset additions.
functions: Create Mass Additions daily at 05:00
Post Mass Additions as needed
Depreciation by book at month end

nodes.title: Receipt accruals
nodes.subtitle: Purchasing
nodes.description: Period-end accrual of uninvoiced receipts, run as one job set.
functions: Transfer Transactions from Receiving to Costing → Create Uninvoiced Receipt Accruals (per bill-to BU)
Uninvoiced Receipt Accrual Report, then Create Accounting (final)
Accrual reverses when the next period opens

nodes.title: Subledger close
nodes.subtitle: BD1–BD4
nodes.description: Subledgers close in sequence.
functions: BD1: Payables and expense reports
BD2: Cash Management; BD3: Procurement and Payables
BD3–4: Fixed Assets

nodes.title: Allocations & intercompany
nodes.subtitle: Calculation Manager
nodes.description: Monthly allocation rules and intercompany billing.
functions: About six allocation rules a month: run, validate, deploy
Payroll and payroll-accrual allocations post by state
Monthly shared-services billing from the Mutual to the Agency

nodes.title: GL close
nodes.subtitle: BD6
nodes.description: The ledger closes on business day 6.
functions: Closed for monetary journals on BD6
May reopen for late statutory entries
Year end: revenue and expense roll to retained earnings when the new year opens

nodes.title: Close checklist
nodes.subtitle: EPM close task manager
nodes.description: The month-end checklist with calendar, owners and sign-off.
functions: Every close task with owner, due date and sign-off
Corporate Accounting signals FP&A when its close is done
Consolidation capability planned

nodes.title: Account reconciliation
nodes.subtitle: ARCS
nodes.description: Balance-sheet reconciliations after close.
functions: Reconciliations loaded and certified each month
Implemented 2021/22
Data loaded through Workiva (OneCloud)

nodes.title: Actuals to Planning
nodes.subtitle: FP&A
nodes.description: FP&A loads actuals and ties the P&Ls.
functions: Loads once or twice a day until the P&Ls tie
Manual journal errors (e.g. missing product) are traced back with Accounting
Pushes the results into OAC Essbase

nodes.title: Publish dashboards & reports
nodes.subtitle: OAC · Narrative
nodes.description: The month is announced closed with dashboards and financial reports published.
functions: Dashboards and financial reports published together
Users reach them from the finance systems landing page
Dashboards are the preferred view over financial statements

integrations.title: Integration register
integrations.lede: Interfaces documented in the source notebook, by name. State as of 2023; a working list, not a certified register.

dashboards.title: Finance dashboards: how they are produced
dashboards.lede: Dynamic reporting (OAC dashboards, Data Visualization, Smart View) draws on Planning, OAC Essbase, Oracle Financials and insurance operations data; static reporting runs in Narrative Reporting (on Essbase) and BI Publisher (non-Essbase). Pick a path to follow it; select any box for details.

legend.label: Data Integration / Data Management / file load

nodes.title: Exceed
nodes.subtitle: policy administration
nodes.description: Insurance operations system: policies, premium, claims and reserves.
functions: Source of the insurance operations data in the dashboards
Daily and monthly figures feed the GL through ADW
Reports historically ran from the BIM database

nodes.title: On-premise warehouse
nodes.subtitle: EDW · BIM · HDS · DWM
nodes.description: SQL Server warehouses holding the insurance data (DWM): loss reserves, premium (GWP, EP, UEP), claims, subrogation and salvage, policy.
functions: Source for ADW through OCI Data Integration
BI Publisher static reports read DWM directly
EDW Finance workgroup receives the budget for Tableau reports

nodes.title: Fusion ERP
nodes.subtitle: GL · AP · procurement · assets
nodes.description: Oracle Fusion Financials: the system of record for balances and transactions.
functions: GL balances feed the Essbase dashboards through the balances cubes
Subledger and GL detail feed the transactional dashboards through OTBI
Receives policy journals (OIC) and allocations (Workiva (OneCloud))

nodes.title: OCI Data Integration
nodes.subtitle: Fast Connect
nodes.description: Moves on-premise Exceed data into ADW (treated as implemented).
functions: Replaced DataSync for the daily insurance feeds
Converted the BIM reports (e.g. six-month auto policy)
Was to trigger both daily jobs: reports and journals

nodes.title: Integration VM
nodes.subtitle: DataSync · Gateway · GroundRunner
nodes.description: Legacy on-premise connectors.
functions: DataSync loaded BIM data to the ADW stage schema
Oracle Data Gateway exposed on-premise data to OAC
GroundRunner ran Workiva (OneCloud) and EPM automation

nodes.title: Workiva (OneCloud)
nodes.subtitle: ETL between Oracle clouds
nodes.description: Integration studio and data prep used for ETL between the finance Oracle cloud systems.
functions: GL trial balances and actuals/budget into Planning
Planning actuals, budget and forecast into the OAC Essbase cubes
Report outputs to the Financials Doc Cloud; budget to the EDW

nodes.title: Oracle Integration Cloud
nodes.subtitle: policy journals
nodes.description: Creates GL journals from the ADW insurance data mart.
functions: Daily premium and commissions, claims, change in case reserves (10:00)
Monthly policy count, advanced premiums, written vs prior written (first 5 days)
Creates unposted GL batches for review and posting

nodes.title: OTBI
nodes.subtitle: subject areas · catalog
nodes.description: Oracle Transactional Business Intelligence: real-time subject areas over Fusion data.
functions: Exposed to OAC as datasets through an OTBI catalog connection
Daily transactional reports start the transactional dashboard refresh
Reports used by dashboards are regression-tested every quarterly update

nodes.title: ADW
nodes.subtitle: FDW · ORAFINANCIALS · insurance mart
nodes.description: Oracle Autonomous Database: the finance data warehouse with transaction-level data.
functions: Finance data warehouse and ORAFINANCIALS schema with OTBI-based Fusion data
Insurance data mart: daily, monthly and stage schemas
Source for transactional dashboards and BI Publisher reports

nodes.title: GL balances cubes
nodes.subtitle: Fusion Essbase
nodes.description: The Essbase balances cubes inside Fusion General Ledger.
functions: Refreshed daily (05:45) by Transfer GL Balances to Balances Cube
Source of trial balances and actuals/budget for Planning
Read by Smart View and Financial Reporting

nodes.title: Planning
nodes.subtitle: Financials · Workforce · Reporting cubes
nodes.description: EPM Planning: Financials BSO (current and prior year), Workforce BSO (budget cycle), Reporting ASO (2010 onward).
functions: Actuals loaded once or twice a day during close until the P&Ls tie
Workforce cubes fed from Core HR through Data Management
Budget and forecast; Capital and Strategic Planning cubes owned by FP&A

nodes.title: OAC Essbase
nodes.subtitle: Financials · Revenue Planning · Analytics · Foundation
nodes.description: The OAC Essbase cubes behind most of the financial dashboards.
functions: Financials cube loaded from Planning (actuals, budget, forecast)
Revenue Planning, Analytics and Foundation cubes
Sends allocations and statistical allocation rates back to GL

nodes.title: OAC BI dashboards
nodes.subtitle: dynamic reporting
nodes.description: Oracle Analytics Cloud dashboards: the preferred way for leadership to see the financials.
functions: Essbase dashboards on the OAC Essbase cubes
Transactional dashboards on OTBI datasets and ADW
Published by FP&A after close and announced

nodes.title: Data Visualization
nodes.subtitle: data flows · datasets
nodes.description: OAC Data Visualization: data flows that shape OTBI and ADW data into dashboard datasets.
functions: Daily OTBI report → data flow → mapped dataset
Examples: AP imaging auditability, procurement and contracts, daily policy-feed status
Analysts can create their own data sources and connections

nodes.title: Smart View
nodes.subtitle: Excel analytics
nodes.description: Smart View for Office: ad hoc analysis on the Essbase cubes.
functions: Connects to the Fusion GL balances cubes and OAC Essbase
Used to build and check allocation rules
Part of the dynamic reporting toolset

nodes.title: Finance systems landing page
nodes.subtitle: single entry point
nodes.description: Landing page linking the Oracle finance systems: Planning, dashboards and reports.
functions: One place to navigate between Planning, OAC dashboards and reports
New reporting functions added as cards
Month-closed announcements point users here

nodes.title: Narrative Reporting
nodes.subtitle: static · on Essbase
nodes.description: EPM Narrative Reporting: management and narrative report packages on Essbase.
functions: Report packages with author, review and sign-off
About 200 reports
Fed from Planning and the GL

nodes.title: BI Publisher
nodes.subtitle: static · non-Essbase
nodes.description: Oracle Analytics BI Publisher: static reports for non-Essbase data.
functions: Written directly against ADW and the on-premise warehouse (DWM)
Daily and monthly report outputs for Accounting
Replaced most legacy Business Objects reports

nodes.title: Financials Doc Cloud
nodes.subtitle: Oracle Content Cloud
nodes.description: Oracle Content Cloud folder where Accounting picks up report outputs.
functions: Receives BI Publisher outputs daily and monthly
Finance security group controls access
One place for Accounting to find the reports

nodes.title: Finance workgroup (Tableau)
nodes.subtitle: on-premise EDW
nodes.description: Tableau reports run by the Finance workgroup on the on-premise EDW.
functions: Receives the budget from OAC Essbase
Reports for audiences outside the Oracle tools
Part of the on-premise warehouse

notes.title: Essbase dashboards.
notes.text: GL balances cubes → Workiva (OneCloud) → Planning → OAC Essbase → dashboards and Smart View. Most financial dashboards follow this path; FP&A publishes them after close.

notes.title: Transactional dashboards.
notes.text: Fusion → OTBI → Data Visualization data flows (and ADW for history and insurance joins) → dashboards. Refreshed daily.

notes.title: Insurance data.
notes.text: Exceed → on-premise warehouse → OCI Data Integration → ADW; OIC turns it into GL journals and BI Publisher into static reports.
